taxonomy.lookalike_taxon_note: Asclepias subverticillata is a separate accepted species, not simply this species under another current name.

target_zone_range.evidence_note: BONAP was reviewed first as the project's primary county-level authority. A USDA-derived Texas county distribution list supports Bell, Gillespie, and Travis. UT's Williamson County flora independently documents Williamson County. This comfortably satisfies the project's >=3 target-zone county threshold.
target_zone_range.correction_note: This supersedes the earlier unresolved pass. Williamson County is part of the project's 25-county target zone, and Bell + Gillespie + Travis provide three additional supported target-zone counties.

morphology_keys.habit: Slender herbaceous perennial, usually about 30–90 cm tall.
morphology_keys.leaf_arrangement: Mostly whorled, commonly 3–4 leaves per node in TPWD's Texas treatment; other references may describe broader variation.
morphology_keys.leaf_morphology: Sessile or nearly sessile; extremely narrow linear to filiform blades, usually somewhat revolute and essentially glabrous.
morphology_keys.inflorescence: Solitary or paired clusters at upper nodes, few- to many-flowered.
morphology_keys.flower_color: Small greenish-white flowers, sometimes externally purple-flushed.
morphology_keys.gynostegium_detail: Corona hoods with horns; flower structure is much smaller and more delicate than broad-leaved milkweeds such as A. viridis.

fastest_traits: Leaves arranged in obvious whorls around the stem
Small greenish-white flower clusters at upper nodes
field_diagnostics.single_best_trait: The combination of extremely narrow linear leaves and true whorled phyllotaxy is the fastest field clue.
field_diagnostics.lookalike_note: A. subverticillata is a distinct accepted western species. Do not collapse the two names in the database.

ecological_notes.texas_habitat: Blackland prairies, coastal prairies, Crosstimbers, Grand Prairie, post oak savannas, pine-oak savannas, and related open habitats; rare in live-oak and post-oak savannas of the Edwards Plateau.
ecological_notes.broader_habitat: Prairies, glades, open woods, rocky or sandy slopes, pastures and roadsides.
ecological_notes.host_status: Native Asclepias and larval host for monarch butterflies; flowers provide nectar for multiple pollinator groups.
